J.'''" '''Liddell Jr.''' (born December 18, 2000) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State Buckeyes]]. ==Early life and high school career== Liddell was raised in [[Belleville, Illinois]], and went to high school at [[Belleville High School-West]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.thelantern.com/2020/09/mens-basketball-e-j-liddell-gets-more-opportunity-to-shine-in-sophomore-campaign/|first=Jack|last=Emerson|title=Men’s Basketball: E.J. Liddell gets more opportunity to shine in sophomore campaign|website=The Lantern}} He averaged 20.8 points and 8.2 rebounds per game as a junior, won the 2018 [[Illinois Mr. Basketball]] award,{{Cite web|url=https://ohiostatebuckeyes.com/roster/e-j-liddell/|title=E.J. Liddell-Ohio State Men’s Basketball|website=Ohio State Athletics}} shared the 2018 ''[[St. Louis Post Dispatch]]'' Player of the Year with [[Courtney Ramey]],{{cite web |last1=Kvidahl |first1=David |title=All-Metro boys basketball co-players of the year: Ramey, Liddell cemented legacies |url=https://www.stltoday.com/sports/high-school/all-metro/boys-basketball/all-metro-boys-basketball-co-players-of-the-year-ramey-liddell-cemented-legacies/article_5d0ea356-3459-11e8-b0d7-ef46d13028e1.html |website=[[St. Louis Post-Dispatch]] |access-date=February 10, 2021 |date=March 31, 2018}} and won the Illinois 4A class state championship.{{Cite web|url=https://buckeyeswire.usatoday.com/2019/03/16/ohio-state-basketball-recruit-e-j-liddells-team-wins-illinois-state-championship/|first=Phil|last=Harrison|title=Ohio State basketball recruit E.J. Liddell's team wins Illinois state championship|website=Buckeyes Wire}} As a senior, he averaged 20.2 points, 9.3 rebounds and 3.8 blocks per game. For the second year in a row, he won Illinois Mr. Basketball,{{cite web|url=https://amp.bnd.com/article228422004.html|first=Dean|last=Criddle|title=Two players have won Mr. Illinois Basketball twice. West’s Liddell is now one of them.|website=Belleville News{{endash}}Democrat}} the ''St. Louis Post Dispatch'' Player of the Year,{{cite web|url= https://www.stltoday.com/sports/high-school/all-metro/boys-basketball/all-metro-boys-basketball-player-of-the-year-belleville-wests-liddell-leaves-a-legacy-few/article_75d023b6-5284-11e9-8050-636eb436d3ce.html|first=David|last=Kvidahl|title=All-Metro boys basketball player of the year: Belleville West's Liddell leaves a legacy few can rival|website=St. Louis High School Sports}} and the Illinois 4A class state championship. ===Recruiting=== Liddell was a consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and ranked the best player in the state of Illinois. On October 1, 2018, Liddell committed to playing college basketball for [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] over scholarship offers from teams such as [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]], [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]], and [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin]].{{Cite web|url=https://amp.bnd.com/latest-news/article219301975.html|first=Dean|last=Criddle|title=EJ Liddell picks Ohio State over Illini, Missouri|website=Belleville News-Democrat}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|collapse=no|year=2019}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = E. J. Liddell | position = [[Power forward (basketball)|PF]] | hometown = [[Belleville, Illinois|Belleville, IL]] | highschool = [[Belleville High School-West|Belleville West]] (IL) | feet = 6 | inches = 7 | weight = 220 | 40 = | commitdate = October 1, 2018 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 4 | 247 stars = 4 | espn stars = 4 | espn grade = 89 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2019 | rivals ref title = Ohio State 2019 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2019 Ohio State Buckeyes Recruiting Class | 247 ref title = | rivals school = ohiostate | 247 school = | espn schoolid = 194 | scout overall = | rivals overall = 41 | 247 overall = 60 | espn overall = 38 | accessdate = March 20, 2021 | bball = yes }} ==College career== [[File:EJ Liddell.jpg|thumb|upright|Liddell with [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] in 2020]] Liddell came off the bench during his freshman year, averaging 6.7 points and 3.8 rebounds per game. He played in all 31 games and was second on the team with 29 blocks.{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/ej-liddell-1.html|title=E.J. Liddell College Stats|website=Sports Reference}} He had a double-double in a win against [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]].{{Cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/ohio-state/Article/Ohio-State-basketball-EJ-Liddell-puts-it-together-in-breakout-performance-vs-Illinois-Fighting-Illini-144685591/|first=Patrick|last=Murphy|title=EJ Liddell puts it together in breakout performance vs. Illinois|website=Bucknuts}} During the early parts of his sophomore season, he contracted [[infectious mononucleosis|mononucleosis]], which led to Liddell being out for several games.{{Cite web|url=https://amp.buckeyextra.com/amp/4021302001|first=Adam|last=Jardy|title=Ohio State's E.J. Liddell full-steam ahead for Big Ten play after playing through illness|website=BuckeyeXtra}} He had another good game against Illinois during his sophomore year, scoring a season-high 26 points in a win.{{Cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/basketball-ncaa-ill-ohs/e-j-liddell-fuels-no-21-ohio-state-past-no-14-illinois-idUSMTZXEH1G1LI755|title=E.J. Liddell fuels No. 21 Ohio State past No. 14 Illinois|website=Reuters}} Liddell averaged 16.2 points, 6.7 rebounds, and 1.1 blocks per game during his sophomore season. After Ohio State's Round of 64 loss to [[Oral Roberts Golden Eagles men's basketball|Oral Roberts]], Liddell received threats from basketball fans via social media. After he posted screenshots of the threats on Twitter, Ohio State reached out to law enforcement regarding the threats.{{cite web |title=Source: Ohio State reaches out to police after E.J. Liddell received threatening tweets following NCAA tournament loss |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31097748/ohio-state-ej-liddell-responds-disgruntled-fans-ncaa-tournament-loss |website=ESPN.com |access-date=March 20, 2021 |date=March 20, 2021}} On March 31, 2021, Liddell declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2939045-ohio-states-ej-liddell-will-enter-name-in-2021-nba-draft|first=Joseph|last=Zucker|title=Ohio State's E.J. Liddell Will Enter Name in 2021 NBA Draft|website=Bleacher Report}} He later withdrew from the draft and announced that would return to Ohio State for his junior season. On January 9, 2022, Liddell scored a career-high 34 points in a 95–87 win against [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern]].{{cite news |title=Liddell leads No. 13 Ohio State past Northwestern 95–87 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401364371 |access-date=January 29, 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=January 9, 2022}} He was named to the First Team All-[[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]].{{cite press release|url=https://bigten.org/news/2022/3/8/2021-22-big-ten-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-announced.aspx|title=2021-22 Big Ten Men’s Basketball Postseason Honors Announced|publisher=[[Big Ten Conference]] |date=March 8, 2022 |accessdate=March 8, 2022}} As a junior, he averaged 19.4 points, 7.9 rebounds, 2.5 assists and 2.6 blocks per game. On March 25, 2022, Liddell declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web |last1=Chavkin |first1=Daniel |title=Ohio State Star Forward E.J. Liddell Announces Decision to Enter NBA Draft|url=https://www.si.com/college/2022/03/25/ej-liddell-ohio-state-declares-nba-draft |website=SI.com |access-date=March 26, 2022 |date=March 25, 2022}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|Ohio State]] | 31 || 0 || 16.6 || .464 || .192 || .718 || 3.8 || .5 || .4 || .9 || 6.7 |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2020–21]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2020–21 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|Ohio State]] | 29 || 29 || 29.4 || .474 || .338 || .746 || 6.7 || 1.8 || '''.7''' || 1.1 || 16.2 |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2021–22]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2021–22 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|Ohio State]] | '''32''' || '''32''' || '''33.2''' || '''.490''' || '''.374''' || '''.765''' || '''7.9''' || '''2.5''' || .6 || '''2.6''' || '''19.4''' |- class="sortbottom" | style="text-align:center;" colspan="2"| Career | 92 || 61 || 26.4 || .480 || .341 || .749 || 6.1 || 1.6 || .5 || 1.6 || 14.1 {{S-end}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://ohiostatebuckeyes.com/roster/e.j-liddell/ Ohio State Buckeyes bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Liddell, E.
